title: Shyam Kumar Awasthi v. U.P.P.C.L.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Tarun Agarwala, J.; Vipin Sinha, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; Executive Engineer to consider objection and pass assessment.
headnote: Provisional bill on a checking report of theft — consumer’s remedy is a reply under s.126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and clause 8.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 — objection already served as a notice to be considered by the Executive Engineer, who shall pass an assessment order — writ disposed without examining the theft finding or quantum.
facts: Following a checking report that recorded theft of electricity, U.P.P.C.L. issued a provisional bill of Rs. 82,451 to Shyam Kumar Awasthi. He filed a civil writ in the Allahabad High Court, having already served a notice of objection (annexure 3). Counsel for both sides were heard. The Division Bench did not try whether theft was made out or whether the billed amount was correct.

holding_units.holding: A consumer objecting to a provisional bill raised on a checking report of theft must file a reply under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and clause 8.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where that objection has already been served as a notice, the concerned Executive Engineer shall consider it and pass an appropriate assessment order; the writ court will not itself decide the assessment.

Clause 8.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003, is the path for a reply to a provisional theft bill; the Executive Engineer must consider the objection and pass an assessment order.

not_decided.point: Whether theft was established and whether the provisional assessment of Rs. 82,451 was correct
not_decided.note: Left to the Executive Engineer on the pending objection.
